description: English decimal point — the mirror image of french-number: stringify, no comma substitution. Do NOT implement this with a locale-aware formatter, for the same reason as french-number: those add thousands separators and vary by platform and OS version. Hand-authored: the sandbox stays French-only and has no English reference implementation to generate this from.
generatedBy: hand-authored — sandbox is out of scope, no reference implementation exists

cases.why: The common case — the dot stays a dot, unlike french-number's comma substitution.
An integer renders "2", not "2.0". A fixed-one-decimal formatter fails here, same as in French.
Renders "0.5" and not ".5". Some locale formatters drop the leading zero for values below one, which is why this is pinned rather than assumed.
The value produced by the 80 g / 64 g portion tie, so this suite joins up with describe-quantity-en the same way french-number does with describe-quantity.
No thousands separator and no space; a locale formatter may insert one.
Zero counts as an integer, so it renders "0" and not "0.0". Reachable whenever an ingredient is scaled all the way down.
